summary.headline: EPACK Prefab Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~25% to INR366 crore, with EBITDA margin down ~100 bps to 9.4% on steel costs and order book at INR1,380 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue grew about 25% YoY to INR366 crore from INR295 crore, and EBITDA rose to nearly INR35 crore from INR30.9 crore. EBITDA margin fell to 9.4% from 10.5%, which management attributed to steel price increases linked to the Middle East conflict, partly offset by fixed-price contract repricing and purchasing policy. Order inflow was INR580 crore versus INR240 crore a year earlier, and the order book stood at about INR1,376-1,380 crore as of 30 June 2026. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,900-1,950 crore (about 30% growth) and a 10.5-11.5% EBITDA margin from Q2 onwards, and announced a data center subsidiary with INR75 crore planned equity.

segments.name: PEB / prefab (structural steel)
segments.commentary: Order book is 100% PEB per management, with energy sector, logistics (22-25% of book), auto (~10%), cement and steel as main end-users. Management expects ~25% growth in this business; the largest single order is INR165 crore from a renewable company.

segments.name: Sandwich panels
segments.commentary: Order book for sandwich panels is about 3.2 lakh sq m on the Mambattu continuous line, or about 4.7 lakh sq m including Greater Noida and Mambattu, per the Q&A. Utilisation was 44% in Q1, and management expects 70-75%+ for FY27.

segments.name: Ethylene/EPS packaging
segments.commentary: Management said EPS business has returned to normalcy with some price and volume increase. It is run on a monthly rolling plan with no pending order book; about INR180-200 crore of FY27 revenue is expected from it.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR1,900-1,950 crore, about 30% growth; prefab expected to grow ~25%.
FY27 order inflow target of INR2,000 crore; management expects more than 50% achieved in H1.
EBITDA margin to normalise to 10.5-11.5% from Q2 FY27; full-year guidance of ~10.5%.

Ghiloth sandwich panel line to be commissioned by end-Q1 FY27 with commercial production from Q2; Mambattu second AP line starting Q2; Gujarat plant (~50,000 tpa) commissioning in Q4 FY27 with production from April 2027.
Peak revenue potential post-expansion of INR2,700-2,900 crore; management sees INR2,300-2,400 crore possible in FY28 at 80-85% utilisation.
capex_capacity: Ghiloth second sandwich panel line (8 lakh sq m capacity) to be commissioned by end of Q1 FY27; each line implies INR125-140 crore panel revenue, or ~INR250 crore with fabrication.
Mambattu (AP) second line expected to start in Q2 FY27.
Gujarat plant (about 50,000 tpa) to be commissioned in Q4 FY27, production from April 2027.
Analyst-cited PEB capacity of ~1,47,000 tpa rising by ~23,600 tpa in FY27 Q2 (management said operational from Q3); management did not confirm these figures.
EPACK Data Center Solutions subsidiary, with INR75 crore proposed equity; the land and facility location are still to be finalised, with numbers expected by end-Q1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Most orders are fixed-price; pass-through is not used. Management says steel prices rose 12-15% since the war began, but the balance-sheet impact was ~1% due to repricing new orders and sourcing.
Average order size in the pending book is INR12-13 crore (FY26 average INR6.5 crore); median is somewhat lower.
Win rate is ~20% (management said 10-12% is typical for peers). Existing-client share of order book is 40-45%; win rate from existing clients estimated at 30-40%, not tabulated.
Organised domestic PEB market share ~5-6% in FY26, targeted at 7-7.5% by FY27-end; market leader ~12%.

Data center: 4-5 projects done on sandwich panels, ~4-5% of order book; Adani order for panels won in Q1; two full-structure data center bids lost on design and pricing; typical data-center building ticket INR60-110 crore.
Exports: first sandwich panel export order (~INR2.5 crore) shipped to Africa; PEB exports limited to SAARC nations; railways business nil.

qa_highlights.question: Share of fixed-price vs pass-through orders in the current book?
qa_highlights.answer: Most orders are fixed-price; management manages risk by booking orders weekly at current prices. Steel rose 12-15% but the balance-sheet impact was about 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 10-11% and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects improvement from Q2 and full-year EBITDA margin of ~10.5%. Q1 dip was ~100 bps against an earlier estimate of ~200 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Data center revenue potential, working capital, and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify until end-Q1 numbers are available and said the funding plan is undecided, with any debt expected to be modest.

qa_highlights.question: Sandwich panel order book fell from 4 lakh to 3.2 lakh sq m QoQ; is utilisation still rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Correction: 4 lakh sq m covered Greater Noida and Mambattu. Mambattu continuous line alone has 3.2 lakh sq m, and total including Greater Noida is about 4.7 lakh sq m. Even without new orders, the line would reach 70%+ annualised utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Win rate of ~20%: what drives the rate and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it bids on 30-40% of quotes and selects projects, and losses come partly from capacity constraints by region. A 20% win rate is said to be strong against 10-12% peers.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company sustain 30% growth beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited India fabrication demand of 12-19% of steel output, ~36 million tonnes by 2030 in the pessimistic case, and suggested EPACK's 0.3-0.35 million tonnes is a small share.

risks_watch: Margin recovery to 10.5-11.5% from Q2 depends on repricing and new orders at post-war steel prices; Q1 margin was 9.4% and management said the impact was about 100 bps versus an earlier estimate of about 200 bps.
Most orders are fixed-price with no pass-through; steel rose 12-15% since the war began. Booking weekly at current prices is the main protection, so a further steel spike could hit margins again.
Data center subsidiary: INR75 crore planned equity, but land, location, capex, funding mix (possible debt) and ROCE are not yet defined; numbers promised by end-Q1 FY27 and next quarter's call.

Capacity ramp-up timing: Ghiloth sandwich panel line due end-Q1 with production from Q2, Mambattu second AP line from Q2, Gujarat (~50,000 tpa) in Q4 FY27 with production from April 2027. Monsoon-related civil works delays were flagged as a Q2 execution risk.

Order book coverage: opening book INR1,110 crore on 1 April 2026 and order book INR1,376-1,380 crore at 30 June 2026 against FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,900-1,950 crore; FY27 order inflow target of INR2,000 crore, with INR580 crore booked in Q1 and management expecting more than 50% in H1. Win rate of about 20% and the sandwich panel order book (3.2 lakh sq m Mambattu line) need to be tracked.

summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year revenue target, order book visibility and a margin rebound from Q2, supported by repricing and new orders at higher steel prices. Noticeably cautious and non-committal on data center economics (revenue, working capital, ROCE, funding, margins), saying numbers will come only by end-Q1.
